payload.objective: Test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human polymyxin B exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation; the primary outcome is model feasibility (SC001).

context_sources.main:/objective: Test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human polymyxin B exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation; the primary outcome is model feasibility (SC001).
context_sources.main:/study/drug: Polymyxin B (PMB), the sole test drug (SC003).
context_sources.main:/study/regimen: Partial, separate dosing information is supplied: mouse dose-fractionation schedules, rat IV administration, and horse single- and repeated-dose summaries and reported doses (SC005, SC006, SC009, SC016).
context_sources.main:/study/population: Mouse, rat and rabbit development evidence; held-out horses; eligible K. pneumoniae PD evidence; and a separate human validation cohort (SC005, SC006, SC007, SC009, SC010, SC011).
context_sources.main:/study/system: Animal-to-human systemic PK translation, supported pulmonary PK, and eligible PK/PD analysis (SC001, SC014, SC019).
context_sources.main:/study/measurements: Described plasma, serum, ELF and tissue PK, binding, MIC, bacterial-burden and human validation measurements (SC005, SC006, SC007, SC010, SC011).
context_sources.main:/study/methods: Prepare source data, fit eligible animal PK models, test frozen scaling in horses, predict human PK, assess PK/PD indices, validate human predictions, then assess PTA and feasibility (SC013, SC014, SC016, SC018, SC019, SC020, SC021).
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/0/stateme: The project will test whether animal PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human PMB exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation. Its primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/1/stateme: PMB is a known-drug test case with existing human PK for independent validation. The project follows the translational objective of Sou et al. (2021) without importing the apramycin model or its parameters.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/2/stateme: PMB is the sole test drug; colistin and other antibiotics are not substitutes.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/3/stateme: PMB_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is described as the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes, not a ready-made modeling dataset.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/4/stateme: The mouse material is described as plasma and ELF PK, serum binding from two conflicting sources, strain MICs, dose-fractionation schedules, bacterial-burden endpoints, and digitized index-response panels, for animal PK and eligible PD analysis. See MI001 for the unverified panel-to-regimen matching.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/5/stateme: The rat material is described as individual IV plasma profiles, serum and seven-tissue biodistribution means, and serum binding by dialysis and ultrafiltration. Its stated uses are systemic PK and supported pulmonary translation; limited observations do not establish predictive validity.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/6/stateme: The rabbit material is described as plasma, ELF and whole-lung mean profiles, exposure summaries, pulmonary infection outcomes, and study metadata. Its component support and source discrepancies are unresolved in MI002 and MI003.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/7/stateme: The proposal reports that no further public rabbit PMB concentration data were found.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/8/stateme: The held-out horse material is described as digitized serum concentrations from two veterinary studies—healthy-horse peaks and troughs and hospitalized-horse daily samples—and printed single- and repeated-dose summaries from a third study. Horse dose-basis and binding issues are recorded in MI004 and MI005.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/9/stateme: The in-vitro material is described as K. pneumoniae time-kill data for BAA1705, KP619 and three KPC-2 isolates at two static concentrations; genotype and MIC data for six carbapenem-resistant isolates; and a surveillance MIC distribution. Eligible time-kill data serve PD analysis, while the distribution serves population-weighted attainment and cannot replace matched strain MICs.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/10/statem: The described human validation cohort has 40 patients, 230 concentration records and 268 dose events; human reference tables are also described. See MI006 for availability and release conditions.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/11/statem: PMB_project_proposal.docx defines the task; AGENT_README.md explains package use and known gaps; benchmark_reference.json is described as final-stage reference material containing published model-derived parameters and targets.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/12/statem: The planned preparation step splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC, validation and benchmark inputs, then checks provenance, units, dose histories, experimental units and missing fields to identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/13/statem: The planned animal PK step selects eligible systemic and, where supported, pulmonary models for mouse, rat and rabbit, evaluating fit, parameter identifiability and held-out prediction where the design permits.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/14/statem: Rabbit evidence may be used only to the extent that it identifies a model component; exclusion or exploratory use must be documented. See MI002 and MI003.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/15/statem: The planned translation uses supported animal models, body size, protein binding and justified physiological relationships, comparing scaling with and without each species rather than assuming that more species is better. After mouse, rat and rabbit scaling is frozen, it predicts horse profiles under reported horse doses, compares them with held-out horse figures as an intermediate large-body-weight translation check, and records the result without retuning.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/16/statem: Horse data must not be used to fit, select or scale models; the held-out horse procedure is specified in SC016.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/17/statem: The project plans to predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC and Cmax with uncertainty under specified doses and routes, then freeze those predictions before opening human outcomes. The required doses and routes are unresolved in MI015.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/18/statem: For eligible K. pneumoniae data, the planned PD analysis compares fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression, estimates supported exposure targets, or reports that the data cannot determine a best index or target.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/19/statem: Human validation is planned by applying the frozen model to actual human dose histories, comparing predicted and observed plasma PK, assessing ELF separately when compatible data exist, and reporting bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/20/statem: After PK validation and PD qualification, the planned PTA step simulates a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, processes the MIC distribution, and includes an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate, uncertainty and the final published-result benchmark where supported. It delivers PTA tables or curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code, or explains why PTA is not estimable if required inputs are missing. SC029 specifies the distinct attainment outputs.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/21/statem: Source identifiers, units, missing values and BLQ limits must be preserved. Group means and digitized observations are not individual animals; IDs, variability, exposure-response links and missing measurements must not be invented.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/22/statem: Routes, formulations, analytes, total versus unbound drug, and plasma, serum, whole-lung tissue, BAL and ELF must remain distinct. Every conversion or physiological bridge requires recorded justification; unsupported pulmonary or multi-species models must not be forced.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/23/statem: The proposal reports conflicting binding sources: mouse about 91% versus 97–99% bound, and rat 80% versus 92–99%.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/24/statem: All three indices and both regression families must have equal eligibility. Comparisons must use the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. The selection rule must be registered before fitting; R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability must be reported with the extra Hill parameter counted. Selection by R² alone and a forced winner are prohibited.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/25/statem: Stasis, 1-log kill and 2-log kill targets must remain separate; other pathogens cannot set K. pneumoniae targets.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/26/statem: Published fitted parameters and model-derived results must remain hidden during primary-analysis selection and cannot set starting values, bounds, priors or rankings; they are reserved for the final benchmark.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/27/statem: Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling. The model, validation criteria, PD targets and MIC input must be frozen before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. If a later model is revised, the original validation result must be preserved.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/28/statem: MIC processing must preserve bins, units, counts or proportions, denominators and censored categories; probabilities must be derived transparently and the MIC distribution frozen. Incomplete coverage must not be silently renormalized, and per-MIC PTA must remain distinct from MIC-weighted attainment.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/29/statem: PTA analysis must include supported PK variability and propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty; group summaries cannot supply invented interindividual variability. Conflicting binding sources must not be averaged, and fu must be carried as a sensitivity parameter.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/30/statem: A successful fit is not predictive validation, and human PK agreement does not validate antibacterial efficacy or safety. Failures and data gaps must be preserved.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/31/statem: Transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results must be saved, and human review must occur before fitting.
context_sources.main:/scientific_context/items/32/statem: The version 3.0 draft, dated 8 October 2026, supersedes earlier versions; prior approvals do not automatically carry forward.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/field: Mouse index-response panel to regimen matching
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/impact: Matched mouse PK/PD comparisons cannot reliably assign the separate panels to regimen records.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/why_it: The proposal explicitly says matching is unverified; attachment bodies have not been assessed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/0/clarif: Establish whether and how each mouse index-response panel matches a dose-fractionation regimen and its response records before matched analysis.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/impact: Rabbit evidence cannot yet be assigned to a supported PK model component rather than exploratory constraints or exclusion.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/why_it: The proposal calls for this assessment during animal PK modeling; the rabbit source data have not been assessed here.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/1/clarif: Assess which, if any, rabbit PK component the described evidence identifies and document exploratory use or exclusion.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/impact: Rabbit source discrepancies cannot be reconciled or carried with precise affected values and scopes yet.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/why_it: The proposal requires preservation of rabbit source discrepancies but does not specify them in the supplied text.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/2/clarif: Identify the rabbit discrepancies from authorized source data, including affected study, matrix, value and consequence.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/impact: Horse dose inputs and exposure comparisons cannot be placed on a verified common mass basis.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/why_it: Horse doses are mostly reported in IU without a salt or base correction.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/3/clarif: For each held-out horse study, establish the reported IU dose meaning and any justified salt or base conversion, retaining unresolved cases.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/impact: Horse unbound-exposure translation cannot use a measured horse binding value from the supplied proposal.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/why_it: The proposal explicitly states that no horse binding is available.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/4/clarif: Document the lack of horse binding and its effect on the held-out horse comparison; use only a subsequently justified basis if one becomes available.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/field: Human validation data availability and release
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/impact: Human observed-outcome validation cannot proceed until the separate data are released under the specified freeze condition.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/why_it: Human validation data are not in this package; the separate file is released only at task 5 after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/5/clarif: At task 5, verify the required freezes and obtain the separately held human validation data without using their outcomes earlier.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/impact: Bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty cannot be judged against fixed criteria until those criteria are specified.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/why_it: The proposal requires criteria fixed before validation but does not give their definitions or thresholds.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/6/clarif: Record the human validation metrics, decision criteria and their freeze before opening human outcomes.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/impact: Mouse free-exposure estimates and translation depend on unresolved source-specific binding values.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/why_it: The conflicting mouse values in SC024 must not be averaged; the proposal requires fu sensitivity.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/7/clarif: Assess the mouse binding sources, conditions and applicable fu sensitivity without silently selecting or averaging them.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/impact: Rat free-exposure estimates and translation depend on unresolved source-specific binding values.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/why_it: The conflicting rat values in SC024 must not be averaged; the proposal requires fu sensitivity.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/8/clarif: Assess the rat binding sources, conditions and applicable fu sensitivity without silently selecting or averaging them.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/field: Qualified K. pneumoniae PK/PD index and targets
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/impact: Target-based dose simulation cannot use a qualified index or exposure target until eligible PD analysis is completed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/why_it: The proposal allows an indeterminate best index or target if available data cannot establish one.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/9/clarif: Compare the eligible indices and regression families under SC019 and SC025, retaining an indeterminate result if warranted.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/impac: Population-weighted attainment cannot be calculated reliably until MIC bins, denominators, censoring and coverage are assessed.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/why_i: The proposal forbids silent renormalization of incomplete coverage; the workbook contents have not been assessed here.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/10/clari: Assess the surveillance MIC distribution and record any incomplete or censored coverage before distribution-weighted PTA.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/field: Support for individual PK variability in PTA
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/impac: The PTA population distribution cannot be specified as supported individual PK variability until its evidence basis is established.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/why_i: The proposal requires supported variability and prohibits inventing interindividual variability from group summaries.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/11/clari: Assess whether defensible individual PK variability can be supported; if it cannot, state the resulting PTA limitation without inventing variability.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/field: Prespecified PTA population and dosing scenarios
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/impac: PTA simulation cannot proceed with defined population and dosing scenarios until they are prespecified.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/why_i: The proposal requires PTA simulation after PK validation and PD qualification, using a population and dosing scenarios prespecified before that simulation; it supplies no scenario choices here.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/12/clari: Specify and freeze the human population and dosing scenarios before PTA simulation.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/impac: The separate ELF validation assessment cannot be performed unless compatible human data exist.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/why_i: The proposal makes ELF assessment conditional, and the protected human file has not been examined.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/13/clari: At validation, determine whether compatible human ELF data exist and either assess them separately or record that this conditional assessment is unavailable.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/14/impac: Human concentration-time, AUC and Cmax predictions cannot be generated under specific regimens until their doses and routes are defined.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/14/why_i: The proposal requests predictions under specified doses and routes but does not specify those values in the supplied text.
context_sources.main:/missing_information/items/14/clari: Specify the human prediction doses and routes before producing and freezing prospective predictions.

project_rules.text: R01: Use PMB as the sole test drug; do not substitute colistin or another antibiotic. Treat the animal and in-vitro workbook as source-shaped tables and notes requiring preparation, not as a ready-made modeling dataset.

evidence.quote: PMB is the sole test drug; colistin and other antibiotics are not substitutes. PMB_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro data workbook. Its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes, not a ready-made modeling dataset:

project_rules.text: R02: Split mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC, validation, and benchmark inputs. Check provenance, units, dose histories, experimental units, and missing fields; identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting. Retain source identifiers, units, missing values, and BLQ limits. Do not treat group means or digitized observations as individual animals or invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links, or measurements.

evidence.quote: Split the mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC, validation, and benchmark inputs. Check provenance, units, dose histories, experimental units, and missing fields. Identify usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

Keep source identifiers, units, missing values, and BLQ limits. Group means and digitized observations are not individual animals. Do not invent IDs, variability, exposure-response links, or missing measurements.

project_rules.text: R04: Hold horse data out of model fitting, selection, and scaling. After freezing mouse, rat, and rabbit scaling, predict horse profiles under reported doses and compare them with the held-out figures as an intermediate translation check; record the result without retuning. Document that horse doses are mostly in IU without salt or base correction and that horse binding data are unavailable.

evidence.quote: Do not use horse data to fit, select or scale models. After the mouse, rat and rabbit scaling is frozen, use them to test whether it predicts a large-body-weight species. Doses are mostly reported in IU without salt or base correction and no horse binding is available; document these limits.

Freeze the scaling, then predict horse profiles under the reported horse doses and compare them with the held-out horse figures as an intermediate translation check; record the result without retuning.

project_rules.text: R06: Keep routes, formulations, analytes, total and unbound drug, and plasma, serum, whole-lung tissue, BAL, and ELF distinct. Record justification for each conversion or physiological bridge. Do not average conflicting mouse or rat binding sources; carry unbound fraction as a sensitivity parameter.

evidence.quote: Separate routes, formulations, analytes, total versus unbound drug, and plasma, serum, whole-lung tissue, BAL, and ELF. Every conversion or physiological bridge requires a recorded justification. Binding sources conflict (mouse about 91% versus 97–99% bound; rat 80% versus 92–99%); never average them, and carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.

project_rules.text: R07: Use eligible K. pneumoniae time-kill data for PD analysis and the surveillance MIC distribution for population-weighted attainment. Do not use that distribution in place of matched strain MICs for exposure-response analysis.

evidence.quote: Use eligible time-kill data for PD and the MIC distribution for population-weighted attainment; it cannot replace matched strain MICs.

project_rules.text: R08: Give fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC, and fT>MIC equal eligibility and compare each using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression. Use the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows, and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability, and identifiability while counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not choose by R² alone or force a winner.

evidence.quote: For eligible K. pneumoniae data, compare fAUC/MIC, fCmax/MIC, and fT>MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression.

Give all three indices equal eligibility and both regression families. Compare them on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows, and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability, and identifiability, counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner.

project_rules.text: R12: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts or proportions, denominators, and censored categories. Derive probabilities transparently, freeze the MIC distribution, and do not silently renormalize incomplete coverage. Report per-MIC PTA separately from MIC-weighted attainment.

evidence.quote: Preserve MIC bins, units, counts/proportions, denominators, and censored categories. Derive probabilities transparently and freeze the MIC distribution; never silently renormalize incomplete coverage. Distinguish per-MIC PTA from MIC-weighted attainment.

project_rules.text: R10: Keep published fitted parameters and model-derived results out of primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors, and rankings; use them for the final benchmark. Do not tune animal models or scaling to human outcomes. Freeze the model, validation criteria, PD targets, and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps, and preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

evidence.quote: Published fitted parameters and model-derived results cannot set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors, or rankings. Keep them for the final benchmark. Human outcomes cannot tune the animal model or scaling. Freeze the model, validation criteria, PD targets, and MIC input before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.

project_rules.text: R11: Access the separately held human validation data only at task 5, after freezing the animal model, scaling, and predictions. Apply the frozen model to actual human dose histories; compare predicted and observed plasma PK, assess ELF separately when compatible data exist, and report bias, precision, exposure agreement, and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.

evidence.quote: Human validation data are not in this package. The 40-patient dataset (230 concentration records, 268 dose events) and human reference tables are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.

Apply the frozen model to actual human dose histories. Compare predicted and observed plasma PK; assess ELF separately when compatible data exist. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement, and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.

project_rules.text: R15: Obtain human review before fitting. This proposal supersedes earlier versions, so do not assume prior approvals carry forward.

evidence.quote: obtain human review before fitting. This proposal supersedes earlier versions; prior approvals do not automatically carry forward.

project_rules.text: R03: Select eligible systemic and, where supported, pulmonary PK models for mouse, rat, and rabbit. Evaluate fit, parameter identifiability, and held-out prediction where the design permits. Use rabbit evidence only insofar as it identifies a model component; otherwise document exclusion or exploratory use, preserving source discrepancies. Do not force unsupported pulmonary or multi-species models.

evidence.quote: Select eligible systemic and, where supported, pulmonary PK models for mouse, rat and rabbit. Evaluate fit, parameter identifiability, and held-out prediction where the design permits. Use rabbit evidence only to the extent it identifies a model component; document exclusion or exploratory use.
Assess whether these support a model component or only exploratory constraints; preserve source discrepancies.
Do not force unsupported pulmonary or multi-species models.

project_rules.text: R14: Interpret fit, prediction, and clinical implications at their respective evidence levels: a successful fit does not establish predictive validation, and agreement with human PK does not validate antibacterial efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps. Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds, and results.

evidence.quote: A successful fit is not predictive validation; human PK agreement does not validate antibacterial efficacy or safety. Preserve failures and data gaps. Save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds, and results

project_rules.text: R05: Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, and justified physiological relationships. Compare scaling with and without each species. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, and Cmax with uncertainty under specified doses and routes, and freeze those predictions before opening human outcomes.

evidence.quote: Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, and justified physiological relationships. Compare scaling with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better.
Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, and Cmax with uncertainty under specified doses and routes, and freeze them before opening human outcomes.

project_rules.text: R09: Estimate only supported exposure targets, or report that the data cannot determine a best index or target. Keep stasis, 1-log kill, and 2-log kill targets separate; targets for other pathogens cannot set K. pneumoniae targets.

evidence.quote: Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that the available data cannot determine a best index or target.
Keep stasis, 1-log kill, and 2-log kill targets separate; other pathogens cannot set K. pneumoniae targets.

project_rules.text: R13: Only after PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios for PTA at each MIC, then report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate only where supported. Include supported PK variability and propagate parameter, binding, PD-target, and MIC uncertainty; do not derive interindividual variability from group summaries. If required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

evidence.quote: After PK validation and PD qualification, simulate a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios to estimate the probability of target attainment (PTA) at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, uncertainty, and the final published-result benchmark. Deliver the PTA tables/curves, feasibility conclusion, and reproducible code; if required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.
Include supported PK variability and propagate parameter, binding, PD-target, and MIC uncertainty; group summaries cannot supply invented interindividual variability.

special_values.MIXED: The item combines several values of this field.
special_values.NOT_FOUND: The source does not state it; not proof that it does not exist.
special_values.NOT_APPLICABLE: The field does not apply to this item.

role.PK_OBSERVATIONS: Measured drug concentrations in a biological matrix at stated times.
role.PD_OBSERVATIONS: Measured effect or response values (for example bacterial counts in vivo) at stated times or exposures.
role.DOSING: Administered dose, route, timing or regimen records.
role.MIC: Minimum inhibitory concentration results with their organism or strain.
role.BINDING: Protein binding or unbound fraction measurements.
role.IN_VITRO_TIME_KILL: In vitro bacterial counts over time under stated drug concentrations.
role.URINE_EXCRETION: Urine concentrations, volumes or amounts excreted over stated intervals.
role.IN_VITRO_CLEARANCE: In vitro metabolic or transport clearance measurements.
role.REPORTED_PARAMETERS: PK or PD parameters as reported by the source, not recalculated.
role.ANIMAL_CHARACTERISTICS: Species, strain, sex, body weight, health or infection state of the animals.
role.MODEL_CATALOG: Descriptions of model structures or model equations.
role.SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE: Methods, assay or context information that supports interpretation but holds no data records.
role.SOURCE_TABLE: A table whose content type the evidence cannot establish; kept as a source table only.

route_category.IV_INFUSION: Intravenous infusion over a stated or unstated duration.
route_category.EXTRAVASCULAR: Any non-intravenous route, such as subcutaneous, intramuscular, oral or intraperitoneal.

matrix_category.INFECTION_SITE: Fluid or tissue at the site of infection, such as epithelial lining fluid or thigh muscle.
matrix_category.OTHER_TISSUE: Any other tissue or body fluid.
matrix_category.IN_VITRO_SYSTEM: Medium or matrix of an in vitro experiment.

record_category.INDIVIDUAL: One record per animal or subject sample. Rows at different times belong to the same animal only when identifiers show it; do not infer serial identity from destructive sampling.
record_category.GROUP_SUMMARY: Mean, median or other statistic over a group of animals or subjects.
record_category.POOLED: Values measured on samples pooled across animals before measurement.

observation_source.SOURCE_VALUES: Values typed in the source table.
observation_source.DIGITIZED_FROM_FIGURE: Values read off a figure by the authors or a later digitization.

column_meaning.TIME: Time of sampling or observation, or interval bounds.
column_meaning.DOSE: Administered dose amount or dose rate.
column_meaning.ANIMAL_ID: Identifier of an animal or subject.
column_meaning.GROUP_OR_TREATMENT: Dose group, treatment arm or experimental condition.
column_meaning.RESPONSE: Measured effect or response, such as bacterial counts.
column_meaning.URINE_AMOUNT: Amount of drug excreted in urine.
column_meaning.PARAMETER_VALUE: Parameter estimates such as AUC, CL or half-life.
column_meaning.SUMMARY_STATISTIC: SD, SEM, CV, range, n or another statistic describing other columns.
column_meaning.BLQ_OR_FLAG: Below-quantification markers, exclusion flags or footnote symbols.
column_meaning.COVARIATE: Body weight, sex, infection state or another subject characteristic.
column_meaning.OTHER: Any other content, including a column whose meaning conflicts across pages.

pk_terminology.use: Read source propositions using this English reference. Terms in a family are related, not interchangeable. Only aliases explicitly map alternative names. Source definitions override conventional symbols; preserve unfamiliar terms too. This is neither a completeness whitelist nor evidence of project facts, selected methods or obligations.

concepts.name: Dose amount
concepts.check: Retain amount, units, formulation and absolute versus body-weight-normalized basis; one administration is not one day.

concepts.name: Dosing schedule
concepts.check: Keep route and schedule with the dose; do not infer either from a concentration curve.

concepts.name: Administration input
concepts.check: Bolus and infusion have different inputs; retain rate and duration separately. Preserve any named extravascular route.

concepts.name: Absorption rate and delay
concepts.check: ka is an absorption rate constant; lag and transit times are distinct delay representations, not elimination half-lives.

concepts.name: Extent of systemic availability
concepts.check: Confirm the source definition and reference route/formulation; do not assign an absolute F from a relative comparison.

concepts.name: Concentration summaries
concepts.check: Retain sampled versus model-derived values and the time window. Cmin is the interval minimum; Ctrough is tied to predose timing. C0 may be extrapolated.

concepts.name: Concentration-time integral
concepts.check: Preserve integration limits, time units, sampling origin and first-dose versus steady-state status. Extrapolated and observed-window exposure differ.

concepts.name: Time-weighted exposure and residence
concepts.check: AUMC is the first moment of the concentration-time curve; MRT is mean residence time. Preserve route, integration window and input-duration correction; MRT is not MTT or half-life.

concepts.name: Repeated-dose exposure
concepts.check: Specify which metric is ratioed and its reference dose/window; a simulated steady-state profile is not an observed one.

concepts.name: Dose-exposure relationship
concepts.check: Retain the normalization denominator and fitted slope/interval. Nonproportional exposure alone does not identify its mechanism.

concepts.name: Clearance measures
concepts.check: Separate systemic, apparent, unbound, renal, hepatic and intrinsic clearance. Bind each to its concentration basis, units and organ/system definition; do not cancel an unknown F.

concepts.name: Distribution volumes
concepts.check: Central, peripheral, steady-state, terminal-phase and apparent volumes differ. V1/V2 labels need the source compartment mapping; Vss alone is not Vc.

concepts.name: Intercompartmental exchange
concepts.check: Confirm the source meaning of Q; organ blood flow may use the same symbol. Exchange clearance and first-order transfer constants have different units.

concepts.name: Elimination and curve slopes
concepts.check: Distinguish model micro-rate constants from hybrid exponential slopes and the estimated terminal slope; compartment assumptions govern any equality.

concepts.name: Half-life
concepts.check: Retain the phase and estimation window. After extravascular dosing, a terminal slope can reflect absorption rather than elimination.

concepts.name: Urinary recovery
concepts.check: Keep collection window and dose denominator; link renal clearance to the matching plasma exposure interval.

concepts.name: Concentration basis
concepts.check: Bound and unbound fractions differ; do not apply an unbound conversion twice or treat nonspecific assay adsorption as protein binding. For fAUC/fCmax, retain the source's free-exposure definition and window.

concepts.name: Binding measurement
concepts.check: Retain matrix, species, method, concentration range and measured versus assumed status; animal binding does not establish human binding.

concepts.name: Site-specific exposure
concepts.check: Keep ratio numerator/denominator, free/total basis and concentration versus AUC basis. Plasma, serum, blood, ELF and homogenate are distinct; retain sampling/dilution corrections.

concepts.name: Susceptibility measurement
concepts.check: Retain isolate, method and conditions. A population MIC90 is not a matched isolate MIC; MIC is not EC50.

concepts.name: Exposure indices
concepts.check: Retain free exposure, MIC pairing and exposure window. Explicitly distinguish duration, fraction and percentage for time above MIC; an index is not its effect target.

concepts.name: Exposure-response models
concepts.check: Keep response definition, sign, units and source parameterization; maximum effect, half-maximal exposure and slope are separate parameters.

concepts.name: Effect target
concepts.check: Retain baseline/comparator and endpoint time; growth inhibition, bacterial killing and resistance suppression are different objectives.

concepts.name: Target attainment
concepts.check: Bind target, regimen, MIC and population assumptions. MIC-specific attainment and MIC-weighted summaries differ; PTA is not cure probability and assumed human IIV remains a scenario.

pk_terminology.supporting_metadata: Bind to drug/analyte, study/analysis, species and subject/group; retain other descriptors only when consequential. Never infer a match from species alone.
data_qualifiers: Preserve units, time origin/window, raw versus digitized and individual versus summary data, sampling unit and n; mean/median and SD/SEM/CV are distinct. Do not infer serial identity from destructive sampling.
Keep BLQ/BQL, LLOQ/ULOQ, LOD, missing and zero distinct; preserve assay limits and missingness reasons. Never invent a limit or treatment policy.

method_knowledge.interpretation: These profiles are project-designed summaries informed by the cited sources, not verbatim guidance or universal regulatory requirements. Use only assigned profiles and assess applicability against the project objective and published rules. Profiles marked DATA_REQUIREMENTS_ONLY report source-backed input coverage and gaps; they do not select analytical methods or qualify results. Prior analytical guidance is retained separately for downstream review and is not loaded into this stage. A profile cannot authorize source access, publish project rules, approve an analysis or impose an unreviewed numeric cutoff. No historical assessment or approval is refreshed automatically. data_roles and condition_triggers let host code map DC labels onto the conditions of profiles already selected from the objective; data never select a profile. A trigger with review OBJECTIVE or DATA, or an undecided label, leaves applicability to the independent coverage review.

profiles.name: Data requirements for animal PK modeling
target_endpoints: animal PK parameters requested by the project
profiles.applies_when: The objective requests an animal time-course model. Check the available modeling inputs and unresolved design information. Model selection, fitting and result evaluation belong to the animal PK module.
required_inputs: Requested modeling objective, parameter or curve outputs and intended use.
Permitted concentration-time observations, dosing events, route, analyte, matrix, concentration basis and units.
Study/regimen membership, sampling design, data level and available experimental-unit identifiers; identify unverifiable IDs rather than inventing them.
conditional_inputs: Infusion duration/input history, extravascular dosing information, or covariates such as body weight when required by the stated objective.
Verified individual-level records and sampling structure when individual or population variability is requested. Do not impose dense repeated sampling for every animal as a universal input rule.
Summary definition, counts and reported variability for group-summary curves; source extraction details for digitized observations; BLQ/LLOQ and missingness metadata where relevant.
Concentration-time data at more than one dose level when the objective includes characterizing dose-dependent (nonlinear) kinetics. Do not impose a number of dose levels.
acceptable_alternatives: Measured group-mean curves may be candidate inputs for exploratory group-level modeling with stated limitations, without inferred animal random effects.
Keep data potentially supporting a separate NCA objective available when modeling inputs are incomplete; do not replace the requested modeling objective silently.
data_checks: Map available concentration, timing, dose, route and grouping information to the stated modeling objective. Report actual coverage and missing phases or dose levels without a universal row-count threshold.
Distinguish individual records, destructive sampling and group summaries. Unverified cross-time IDs do not establish individual trajectories.
Keep study and regimen identities. Identify compatibility questions for later model design; do not pool incompatible sources or treat every source curve as a separate mandatory model.

If input sufficiency depends on a structural model or numerical assessment, retain the uncertainty for the animal PK module. Do not choose compartments, error models, estimation engines or diagnostic thresholds here.
profiles.missing_effect: Report available modeling inputs, task-specific gaps and the data or clarification needed. A positive input assessment permits the next preparation/design step only and does not approve fitting or its results.
not_established: An accepted structural model, convergence, parameter identifiability, uncertainty or a valid human prediction.
Animal IIV from group means or unverified IDs.
Automatic preference for additional compartments or a completed model comparison.
outputs: Endpoint-specific input requirement and matched source evidence
Input availability status, limitations and unresolved definitions
Missing material, affected task or endpoint, required phase and next action

profiles.name: Data requirements for PK/PD indices and PD targets
target_endpoints: Project-requested PD target estimation or use
outputs: Conditional MIC, threshold and PD-target input coverage and gaps
profiles.applies_when: The project requests exposure indices, response-linked index comparison, PD target estimation or a target for later PTA. Distinguish exposure summaries, index ranking and PD target tasks. Reuse existing PK, unit, provenance and MP007 binding assessments rather than repeating them.
required_inputs: The project-defined task and candidate index definitions, exposure windows and concentration basis; specify whether MIC normalization is intended.

For exposure calculations or response-linked fits: source-linked PK observations or reported exposure inputs relevant to the requested indices, retaining their existing evidence status and unresolved prerequisites.
conditional_inputs: For exposure-response analysis, index ranking or estimation of a new PD target: the measured PD endpoint, baseline/comparator, response observation time/window and source, plus traceable mapping among regimen, exposure and response.

If PD target estimation or PTA is requested, specify the desired effect and endpoint window. Identify either a source-supported same-drug target or the matched exposure-response data intended for downstream target estimation. For a reported target, retain its value, index definition, units, free/total basis, exposure window, source and applicability context. A target awaiting estimation is a planned upstream output, not automatically missing data.
For a time-above-threshold index: the threshold and its definition, exposure profile input, analysis window and whether the output is a duration or percentage. A bare fT label is incomplete.

Strain-matched MIC only when an index is MIC-normalized or uses MIC as its threshold, with its units, source and measurement context: method, medium, testing standard, number of replicates and the summary value used (for example the modal value).
For free-exposure indices: use the relevant direct free-concentration or binding-input assessment under MP007.

For in vivo infection-model response data used for index ranking or target estimation: organism and strain identity, inoculum and infection site, host immune status, the interval between infection and treatment start, treatment duration, the response endpoint and its reference point (for example change from treatment start or from an untreated control, or survival), and untreated growth-control data. Keep each combination of treatment duration and endpoint distinct.
acceptable_alternatives: Explicitly requested non-MIC-normalized exposure summaries do not require MIC merely because this is a PK/PD task.
When response data or matching are unavailable, retain independently supported exposure-summary tasks and the unresolved ranking objective.
In vitro response data may be registered for their own stated analysis context, without relabeling them as animal efficacy.
data_checks: Identify whether the task is exposure calculation, index ranking, PD target estimation or use of an existing target. Require matched response data for ranking or new target estimation; do not automatically require raw response data when only a source-supported target is requested.
Check each index definition and window. Do not infer MIC normalization, an fT threshold or duration-versus-percentage meaning from an abbreviated label.
For response-linked tasks, map regimen, exposure and PD observations using source-supported relationships. Preserve ambiguity rather than inventing pairs.
For MIC-dependent tasks, verify that the susceptibility input refers to the relevant strain and measurement context. Do not borrow another drug's MIC or PD target to fill gaps.

For target tasks, distinguish the measured PD endpoint, desired effect and required index value. Record source-supported target inputs separately from planned estimation outputs. Map a documented later target output to DEFERRED with its producing task and required phase; report missing source data or undefined effects/windows separately. This step does not estimate or qualify the target or establish its applicability to human PTA.

For index ranking, record whether the regimens vary dosing frequency or interval in addition to total dose, so that the candidate indices do not change only together. If the design does not separate them, keep the ranking unresolved. Do not impose a numeric count of regimens or dose levels.

When exposure for the PD regimens comes from separate PK data, check whether those data match the PD experiment in species, strain, infection or health state, route and dose range. Record any mismatch as an applicability question; do not assume exposure transfers between animal states.
Report available, absent and unresolved inputs separately by task. Do not fit Emax/Hill models, compute fit statistics or select a winning index in this stage.
profiles.missing_effect: Report which index input or exposure-response mapping is missing through the general data-gap policy. Missing PD matching does not block independent PK or exposure-summary work, but exposure values alone do not establish a best index. An uncomputed target with a documented estimation plan is a deferred output. Preserve any missing target definition or estimation inputs as task-specific gaps; do not make them blockers for independent animal PK or exposure-summary tasks.
not_established: A fitted exposure-response relationship, best index, PD target or evidence of clinical efficacy.

profiles.name: Cross-species data coverage
outputs: Translation-specific missing inputs and required phase
profiles.applies_when: The project requests animal-to-human parameter translation. Reuse the per-species input inventory and definitions assessed under MP003 and applicable profiles; assess only the additional cross-species coverage needs.
required_inputs: The existing parameter-by-species input inventory with source and review status; reuse MP003 definitions and the DR/DC requirement and matching rules instead of re-extracting or repeating them.
The project-specific translation objective and any published species-coverage requirement, including the phase at which it applies.
conditional_inputs: Additional correction factors, calibration evidence or other inputs required by a translation approach explicitly considered in the project. Refer binding and in vitro input details to their relevant profiles; do not select a method or require every possible method here.
Actual body weight for each contributing species and study, with its source, when a considered translation approach scales by body size. Do not substitute typical or textbook weights.
acceptable_alternatives: Retain the source and review statuses already assigned under MP003. Uncomputed source data and unqualified reported estimates may contribute to candidate coverage without becoming qualified parameters.
data_checks: Summarize candidate coverage separately for each parameter and distinct species. Multiple studies, doses, curves or publications from one species do not create additional species.

Use the existing parameter definitions, units and study metadata to flag cross-species comparability questions. Do not repeat their extraction or silently treat incompatible definitions as interchangeable.
Identify only the extra inputs required by explicitly considered translation approaches; retain unresolved approach-dependent needs as questions for the translation module.

Report candidate coverage against any project-specific species requirement, keeping candidate counts separate from later confirmed qualified-species counts. Do not turn a before-translation requirement into a blocker for supported upstream data preparation or animal analysis.
Record the health or infection state of the animals behind each candidate parameter. Parameters from animals in different states are a comparability question, not interchangeable inputs.
profiles.missing_effect: Report affected parameters, coverage gaps and translation-specific missing material through the general data-gap policy. Retain supported upstream work; final parameter qualification and species-count acceptance occur before translation.
not_established: A universal species minimum, qualified parameters, an approved extrapolation method or a validated human prediction.

profiles.name: Human PK simulation input definitions
target_endpoints: Project-requested prospective human IV concentration-time scenarios
outputs: Scenario-specific missing definitions and required phase
profiles.applies_when: The project requests a prospective human IV PK curve. Reuse the registered parameter definitions, units, provenance and gaps; inspect only the additional simulation-scenario definitions and input sources.
required_inputs: The proposed human IV regimen: dose and dose basis, bolus or infusion, applicable infusion duration, and repeat-dosing interval/count where relevant. Unspecified choices remain unresolved.
The requested curve concentration basis and simulation time horizon, sourced from the project objective or an authorized scenario definition.
An input-source inventory distinguishing existing inputs, predicted parameters planned from the translation branch, and inputs with no identified source.
conditional_inputs: Target human body weight or other scenario descriptors only when required by the intended dosing/scaling task; do not insert typical values by default.
For an unbound curve, link the applicable binding-data requirement to MP007 rather than repeating its detailed checks.
acceptable_alternatives: A planned output from the translation branch is a pending input, not missing raw data or an already available qualified estimate. Record its producer and the phase when it is needed.
data_checks: Check whether regimen and curve definitions are explicit and consistent with the requested scenario; list unresolved choices without selecting them.

Reuse prior parameter/source assessments and distinguish prospective human predictions from animal estimates and target-drug human observations. Apply existing project source permissions; do not request target-drug human in vivo PK observations merely to complete a prospective scenario.

Distinguish inputs already supplied, planned downstream outputs and unidentified sources. Do not require an accepted human structure, a complete predicted parameter set or a completed simulation at this stage.

Keep simulation settings such as plotting time-grid resolution for the execution module. Record missing scientific scenario definitions as needed before simulation, without blocking otherwise supported animal data preparation.
profiles.missing_effect: Report missing scenario definitions and input sources with their affected scenario and before-simulation timing. Use the general data-gap policy; preserve supported upstream animal work.
not_established: A selected human model, accepted parameters, a simulated curve, quantified human variability or human predictive validation.

profiles.name: Data requirements for binding and unbound exposure
target_endpoints: Project-requested unbound exposures or binding corrections
outputs: Affected unbound endpoint and missing supporting material
profiles.applies_when: Enable only when the objective requests unbound exposure or a binding correction. Reuse the registered analyte, species, matrix and source metadata; inspect only binding-specific input definitions and coverage.
required_inputs: The requested use and whether the supplied evidence is directly measured unbound concentration, an unbound fraction (fu) or a bound fraction. Preserve explicit percentage versus fractional-scale definitions.

For binding evidence used as an input: reported measurement method, the species and matrix in which binding was measured, experimental conditions including temperature and pH where reported, and concentration range, linked to the existing source and biological-context metadata.
conditional_inputs: Blood/plasma partition information only when the intended task changes the concentration basis between blood and plasma.
acceptable_alternatives: Directly measured unbound concentrations may supply an unbound-exposure input without requiring fu solely for a total-to-free conversion.
Reviewed human-source in vitro binding evidence may be a candidate input when the published project permissions allow its use at the intended stage.
data_checks: Distinguish free concentration, unbound fraction and bound fraction, including percent versus fractional scale. Flag ambiguous definitions rather than guessing or converting them here.

Check whether measurement method, conditions and concentration range are recorded and relevant to the intended use. Preserve concentration-specific records and unresolved applicability; do not assume one value applies to every concentration or matrix.

For separation-based methods such as ultrafiltration or equilibrium dialysis, record any reported nonspecific binding, recovery or mass balance. Missing recovery information is a gap, not evidence that the value is accurate.

Identify only the missing input for the requested unbound endpoint or correction. Do not fit a binding model, perform a concentration conversion or assess conversion sensitivity in this stage.
